title: immutable-ephemeral-witness-protocol-prd-idea
body:
Summary:
This PRD sketch proposes an Immutable Ephemeral Witness (IEW) protocol for Private deployments (customer-managed networking) to give both customers and Redwood a compact, tamper-evident record of network-affecting changes and the associated approval gating without retaining full, long-lived raw telemetry.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers running Redwood Private want verifiable evidence that configuration changes, operator actions, and control-plane approvals occurred according to agreed processes, but many already object to wholesale long-term retention of raw syslogs/pcaps for privacy/compliance reasons.
- Current approval/audit approaches either: 1) retain verbose logs (expensive + privacy surface), or 2) emit sparse approval markers with no strong cryptographic link back to the observed system state. Both create gaps for post-incident forensics and compliance audits.

Proposal (high-level):
Introduce a compact, content-addressed witness artifact that is:
- generated on each control-plane change event (operator action, config commit, approval gate decision),
- includes a short, privacy-minded snapshot (state digests + compressed delta) plus provenance metadata,
- signed by ephemeral witness key(s) and optionally by a customer-side escrow key, and
- stored in two places with different retention semantics: a short-term forensic cache (30–90 days) and a compact immutable index (indefinite, tiny).

Key differentiators vs. existing approaches:
- Minimizes retained PII/telemetry: snapshots are digests + minimal deltas rather than raw packets or full configs.
- Tamper evidence: artifacts are content-addressed (SHA-256) and signed; an immutable index records the artifact hashes with a monotonic sequence number and timewindow timelock.
- Customer control: customers can supply an optional escrow public key so they hold a second signature, enabling cross-verification without Redwood retaining extra data.
- Approval timelock: approve-or-revert windows are recorded as metadata and encoded into the witness artifact to enable reproducible timelines during audits.

Primary goals:
- Provide verifiable evidence for compliance audits that is compact and privacy-friendly.
- Preserve the ability to reconstruct meaningful change narratives (who, what, when, evidence hashes) without storing raw telemetry long term.
- Support automated approval gating and human escalations with a clear, auditable timeline.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for detailed incident response retention where customers explicitly opt to collect PCAPs or extended logs.
- Not intended to be a full PKI or long-term key custody product — keys are ephemeral or optional escrow only.

User stories:
- As a security officer (customer), I want a compact signed artifact I can hand to an auditor proving a change was authorized within the agreed SLO window.
- As a SRE (Redwood), I want to prove we honored a customer-approved fallback policy for a risky operator action.
- As a compliance reviewer, I want to validate a chain-of-custody for a network operator intervention without seeing raw customer traffic.

Design: artifact structure (compact description)
- artifact_version: v1 (string)
- sequence_id: monotonic integer assigned by control plane (string)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 (string)
- change_type: enum (network-rule-update, route-insert, firewall-modify, operator-login, rollback) (string)
- actor_id: user/email or internal operator id (string)
- approval_state: enum (requested, approved, expired, cancelled, auto-fallback) (string)
- timelock_window: {start_iso, end_iso, policy-reference} encoded as single compact field (string)
- state_digest: SHA256(hex) of canonicalized minimal-state JSON (string)
- delta_summary: gzip(base64) compressed minimal diff of key fields (string)
- witness_signatures: list of signature blobs (base64) (list of strings)
- optional_customer_escrow_sig: base64 (string or empty)
- short_audit_note: free-text (string)
- artifact_hash: SHA256(hex) over canonical artifact bytes (string)

Note: artifact fields above are conceptual; actual on-disk artifact will be a compact newline-delimited JSON for easy parsing. We must avoid embedding full configs as plaintext — only canonical minimal-state digests and deltas.

Protocol flow (simplified):
1) Operator submits change to control plane UI/API. Control plane computes canonical minimal-state snapshot for affected resources and the delta summary.
2) An evidence artifact is assembled with the metadata above. A short human note is encouraged (reason, related ticket).
3) An ephemeral witness key (generated periodically by Redwood edge service, rotated frequently) signs the artifact. If customer provided escrow public key, the control plane bundles the artifact for the customer to sign within the timelock window.
4) Artifact is stored in forensic cache (encrypted-at-rest) and the artifact_hash + sequence_id + timestamp is appended to the immutable index. The index entry is also signed.
5) If approval is required by policy, the artifact enters a timelock window. Approvers can sign/approve via the UI; their signatures are appended to the artifact. If approved within window, action proceeds; if window expires, fallback policy kicks in (automated rollback or reduced-scope apply) and that outcome is recorded as a new artifact linked to the original.
6) For audits, auditors request artifact_hashes or the full artifact (depending on customer consent). The immutable index allows quick verification of integrity without retrieving big objects.

Retention and storage model:
- Forensic cache: stores full compact artifacts for 30–90 days (configurable per customer). Encrypted-at-rest; access controlled by RBAC + audit log.
- Immutable index: tiny entries (artifact_hash, seq_id, timestamp, change_type) stored indefinitely. Index is append-only; old purge of index entries only under explicit legal process and always with customer notification.
- Emergency archival: customer can request extended retention for a subset of artifacts (e.g., during active incident) — exported and optionally sent to customer-owned S3.

Privacy & minimization:
- Artifacts must avoid shipping raw customer payloads. Deltas limited to configuration-level keys and resource identifiers; any sensitive fields (IP addresses, user identifiers) must be tokenized or hashed unless explicitly allowed by customer opt-in.
- Redaction policy: when generating delta_summary, fields marked as PII by customer schema will be omitted and replaced with field-level digests.

Operator UX and developer ergonomics:
- UI shows a small "evidence preview" when submitting changes: what minimal state will be captured (digest + delta size), timelock window, and whether customer escrow signing is enabled.
- CLI/API returns artifact_hash immediately on change submission; approval APIs accept signatures in base64 and return updated artifact metadata.
- Search: lightweight index search across seq_id, actor_id, change_type, and a short text in short_audit_note. Full artifact retrieval gated by RBAC and customer consent.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment): Implement IEW synthetic mode where artifacts are produced but only stored locally in a sandbox and not used for real approvals. Collect telemetry on artifact sizes and signature latency. 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (pilot): Offer to 3 customers under NDA who require compact audit proofs. For pilot, default forensic cache = 90 days, immutable index retention infinite. 6–8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): Expose retention config, escrow key onboarding UX, and per-tenant key rotation docs. Integrate with Redwood Console search and audit export. 8–12 weeks after pilot adjustments.

Success metrics:
- Artifact generation latency: 95th percentile < 200ms added to control-plane change path.
- Average artifact size (compressed): target < 4 KB.
- Percentage of requested artifact retrievals that validate via index only (no full artifact fetch): > 70% after GA.
- Customer satisfaction score from pilot auditors: >= 8/10 on usefulness for audits.

Open questions / risks:
- Key management: who owns ephemeral witness keys? If Redwood retains them, do customers consider that acceptable for compliance? Provide clear KMS options and optional customer-supplied escrows.
- Legal: indefinite immutable index retention may be problematic in some jurisdictions — need jurisdictional retention policies and deletion workflows.
- Attack surface: compressed deltas may still leak metadata; need rigorous schema to minimize leakage and a review checklist.
- Sequence monotonicity guarantees across distributed control-plane replicas — need to ensure global ordering or a plausibly monotonic hybrid (leader-assigned seq_id).

Next steps (immediate):
- Engineering spike to implement artifact assembly + signing PoC (owner: Evan Brooks, 1 sprint).
- Security review of delta schema and sample artifacts (owner: Lina Chen, 1 week).
- Legal/Privacy consult on indefinite index semantics and visibility (owner: Priya Raman, schedule meeting).
- Pilot candidate outreach: identify 2–3 customers that run Private and have compliance needs (owner: Miguel Torres, 2 weeks).

Appendix: quick example artifact (newline-delimited compact JSON representation; sensitive fields redacted here):
{\n"artifact_version":"v1",\n"sequence_id":"12587",\n"timestamp_utc":"2025-11-03T17:22:40Z",\n"change_type":"firewall-modify",\n"actor_id":"op+jeff@redwood.ai",\n"approval_state":"approved",\n"timelock_window":"2025-11-03T17:00:00Z/2025-11-03T17:30:00Z|policy:FR-1",\n"state_digest":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...",\n"delta_summary":"H4sIAAAAAAAAE/NIzcnJVwjPL8pJAQAA//8BAAD//w==",\n"witness_signatures":["MEUCIQD...base64sig..."],\n"optional_customer_escrow_sig":"",\n"short_audit_note":"reduced rule scope to remove exposed port for svc-42",\n"artifact_hash":"7a1b2c3d4e5f..."\n}

(above is illustrative; actual artifact will not include raw IPs or full ACL rows unless customer opt-in).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a compact, speculative draft. Feedback requested on:
- delta schema boundaries: which fields are safe to include vs hash/tokenize,
- acceptable retention windows for organizations across NA/EU/APAC, and
- UX patterns to present "minimal evidence capture" to operators without causing approval friction.

-- Priya
